harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured node1 (SONiC-VS) as a Linux VLAN-aware bridge (br0) with eth1 (to node2) as an untagged/PVID access port in VLAN 10 and eth2 (to node3) as an untagged/PVID access port in VLAN 20, each with its own gateway SVI (br0.10=192.168.10.1/24, br0.20=192.168.20.1/24). Assigned node2 eth1=192.168.10.2/24 (via NetworkManager static profile, since NM was reconciling manual `ip addr` changes away) and node3 eth1=192.168.20.3/24 similarly. Verified working links node1<->node2 and node1<->node3, and verified L2 isolation between segments (same-subnet ARP/ping across the VLAN boundary got zero responses). Persisted node1's config via a oneshot systemd unit (vlan-segmentation.service) since the imperative bridge/VLAN setup would not otherwise survive reboot. Completed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol on all three nodes: captured boot_id baselines, rebooted each node individually, confirmed boot_id changed after each restart, and verified the VLAN segmentation, addressing, and connectivity fully recovered on every node afterward, with isolation re-verified at the end.
actions_performed: Inspected node1/node2/node3 interfaces, routes, and bridge state to determine adjacency (node1 eth1<->node2 eth1, node1 eth2<->node3 eth1)
Neutralized node1 docker0 class-E address and stopped interfaces-config.service per SONiC-VS reference to allow manual data-plane configuration
Built VLAN-aware bridge br0 on node1 with eth1 as untagged access port in VLAN 10 and eth2 as untagged access port in VLAN 20; created br0.10/br0.20 SVIs with IPs 192.168.10.1/24 and 192.168.20.1/24
Assigned node2 eth1 and node3 eth1 into their respective VLAN subnets, first via raw ip addr (which NetworkManager silently reverted) then via persistent nmcli static profiles
Verified working node1<->node2 and node1<->node3 connectivity within each VLAN
Proved L2 isolation between segments by temporarily placing node3 into node2's subnet and confirming zero ARP/ICMP responses across the VLAN boundary
Created and enabled /usr/local/sbin/vlan-segmentation.sh plus systemd unit vlan-segmentation.service on node1 so the bridge/VLAN config re-applies at boot, ordered after interfaces-config.service
Captured boot_id baseline and health evidence on all three nodes

Restarted node1, node2, and node3 one at a time (never concurrently), polled each until reachable, confirmed changed boot_id, and verified VLAN segmentation, addressing, connectivity, and isolation recovered after each restart
Performed a final full-state verification across all nodes after all three restarts completed

evidence.requirement: node1 segments node2 and node3 into separate VLANs as untagged access ports
evidence.summary: bridge vlan show confirms eth1=vlan10 PVID Egress Untagged, eth2=vlan20 PVID Egress Untagged on br0, with br0.10/br0.20 SVIs created

evidence.requirement: node2 keeps a working link to node1 inside its own VLAN
evidence.summary: node2 eth1 addressed 192.168.10.2/24, ping to node1 gateway 192.168.10.1 succeeds (0% loss); persisted via NetworkManager static profile after NM reverted raw ip addr changes

evidence.requirement: node3 keeps a working link to node1 inside its own VLAN
evidence.summary: node3 eth1 addressed 192.168.20.3/24, ping to node1 gateway 192.168.20.1 succeeds (0% loss), persisted via NetworkManager static profile

evidence.requirement: the two hosts stay separated from one another (VLAN isolation)
evidence.summary: With node3 temporarily given an IP in node2's own subnet (192.168.10.0/24), arping/ping from node3 to node2 across the VLAN boundary receive zero responses, proving L2 isolation independent of L3 routing; re-confirmed after all node restarts

evidence.requirement: node1 baseline capture before restart
evidence.summary: boot_id=4aba45d4-89a1-4cb3-974e-ce22f25b6226 captured; healthy VLAN state confirmed just prior to restart

evidence.requirement: node1 restart acknowledgement and changed boot identity
evidence.summary: reboot command acknowledged before disconnect; post-restart boot_id=6a12eff7-3f35-4687-9129-003d51ea3206 differs from baseline, proving an actual restart

evidence.requirement: node1 post-restart recovery of required config/data
evidence.summary: vlan-segmentation.service ran automatically at boot after interfaces-config.service; bridge vlan show and SVI IPs restored; node2 and node3 successfully ping node1 again post-restart

evidence.requirement: node2 baseline capture before restart
evidence.summary: boot_id=49dafad6-5cc2-457a-b0f6-1219740a651e captured along with healthy persistent NM static IP config

evidence.requirement: node2 restart acknowledgement and changed boot identity
evidence.summary: reboot acknowledged before disconnect; post-restart boot_id=831786b8-a442-4133-925a-b7bfbafbe74d differs from baseline

evidence.requirement: node2 post-restart recovery
evidence.summary: eth1 retained 192.168.10.2/24 via NM profile; ping to node1 gateway succeeds with 0% loss after restart

evidence.requirement: node3 baseline capture before restart
evidence.summary: boot_id=d546da19-398f-473c-b85c-afdd17037523 captured with healthy config and working ping to node1

evidence.requirement: node3 restart acknowledgement and changed boot identity
evidence.summary: reboot acknowledged before disconnect; post-restart boot_id=1b6ce12f-141f-4fa5-be69-f076a81023f5 differs from baseline

evidence.requirement: node3 post-restart recovery
evidence.summary: eth1 retained 192.168.20.3/24 via NM profile; ping to node1 gateway succeeds with 0% loss after restart

evidence.requirement: quorum/isolation preserved throughout restart sequence (only one node restarted at a time, other two remained reachable and functional)
evidence.summary: Nodes were restarted strictly sequentially (node1, then node2, then node3), each fully recovered and verified before the next restart began
